small_guidance: The mean-subtraction step uses BN running stats during eval, but the harness runs in training mode where BN uses *batch* statistics. Currently the kernel computes mean/var via y.mean/y.var on the conv output, then applies scale/shift, but the subtraction of spatial-mean is applied AFTER the affine — matching the reference. The small numerical drift (~3e-3) suggests fp32 reduction order in y.mean/var differs slightly. Try computing per-channel mean/var inside a Triton kernel with higher-precision accumulation, or use torch.batch_norm directly to get bit-identical BN behavior, then only fuse the spatial-mean subtraction.
large_guidance: Redesign to call F.batch_norm (or torch.batch_norm) for the BN step so training-mode batch stats match the reference exactly, then implement only the spatial-mean subtraction as a Triton kernel (one program per (N,C), two-pass: sum then subtract). Keep the custom ConvTranspose3d kernel as the heavy-op replacement. This eliminates the tolerance gap caused by recomputing batch stats with a different reduction order.
